limits: The five pinned raw GitHub README references for Deep Agents, DeerFlow, OpenHands SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework and OpenHands Agent Canvas were attempted but returned cache-miss fetch failures. Their contents could not be independently reread; retained local source reviews and source metadata were inspected.
This verdict reviews retained evidence; no new native worker, framework installation or head-to-head execution was performed.
Private original streams and host state were not inspected. Public receipts and bounded documentation sections support the historical observations.
The precise underlying model identifier and configured reasoning effort were not exposed to this lane.
open_gaps: No matched execution across the framework candidates establishes superior task quality, ownership preservation, recovery or complete operating cost.

Claude's owned-child repair and graceful Workflow recovery are local integration qualifications. The separate systemd-assisted crash experiment uses a synthetic local effect and does not transfer its guarantees to Workflow.
Host reboot, independent-host restoration, remote provider cancellation, billing cessation and external exactly-once effects remain unqualified.
The accepted inherited-tool role is not an OS sandbox; restricted-role failures remain relevant.
Worktrunk isolates edits, not accounts, permissions or shared services. Its Rust suite was not run, and broader crash cleanup remains unqualified.
The writing comparison passed independent code checks but retained procedural failures in both arms; Workflow used more reported tokens. Recovery usage remains incompletely reconciled.
Codex's retained review and source-task evidence does not establish every Codex child configuration or the same recovery guarantees demonstrated for Claude.

arms: Accepted native Claude worker path with owned worktrees and independent review; retain Codex review as a separately identified operation.
One pinned alternative implementing the same frozen task, owned-path contract, failed-result retention and review gate under declared account and permission settings.
overturn_protocol.metric: Require unchanged task-oracle success, exact owned-path preservation, retained failed results, review before integration, checkpoint/effect correctness and owned-process cleanup. Compare complete elapsed time and non-overlapping usage only where coverage is established; promote for a demonstrated required capability or measured improvement without contract regression.

overturn_when: Execute matched native tasks using blueprints/convergence-practice/native-worker/README.md and the cancellation/continuation cases in blueprints/convergence-practice/worker-recovery/README.md. Change the selection if an alternative passes the same ownership, failure-retention, review and recovery contract while demonstrating a required capability or measured quality/cost improvement. Offline artifact replay alone cannot overturn it.
why_selected: Select complementary native execution and ownership capabilities. blueprints/convergence-practice/native-worker/README.md records an actual Claude child repairing only its owned planner.py, passing twelve unchanged tests and independent exhaustive checks while the primary checkout remained clean. docs/native-workflow-writing-recovery-20260921.md records native execution within a local integration fixture: a stopped reviewer remained failed with a null result, replay reused implementation, and reviewed integration preserved later user edits. Worktrunk's native create/select/list/remove behavior appears in docs/token-native-saturation.md; catalogs/foundation/decisions.json records dirty removal refused without loss, and docs/full-stack-convergence.md reports an old/new comparison correcting child working directory. Codex contributes retained native review: evidence/artifacts/foundation-rd-20260921/native-review.json records a successful three-file review through the optional companion with the review checkout unchanged. These observations support bounded delegation, owned edits and relevant review; they do not establish universal runtime superiority.
